s0423:
[[**86%**]] of Russians see motherhood as hard work, and [[**39%**]] say being a mother is harder today than 20 years ago.

Russian studies also document parental stress, especially emotional exhaustion among mothers. So moms particularly value solutions that take some of the load off.
s0424:
Mindful motherhood means trying to control every risk: finances, pregnancy, housing, parenting know-how, every detail of raising their child.

Medicines too: mom listens to the doctor but double-checks and compares everything.
s0425:
“Smart consumption” is growing in Russia. Parents are less likely than others to buy on price alone: the balance of price, quality and reliability matters more.

For a baby medicine, this is especially true.
s0422: Parenting is getting more intensive: read up, know everything, support development, feed and treat the right way, miss nothing. Intensive parenting attitudes are linked to higher parental stress, mindful parenting to lower stress. So messaging that pushes “you must do it right” even harder can add to the strain.
